items.prompt: I can ___ the boats on the sea.

options.why: Sea is the salty water where the boats sail.
Seas means more than one sea.
Seen needs a helper word, as in I have seen.

hints: The missing word is something you do with your eyes.
See and sea sound the same but have different spellings.
Read the sentence with each word. Which one is about looking?
items.explanation: See means to look with your eyes. Sea is the water where the boats are.

options.why: To is used in phrases like go to school.
Too means also, or very.
Tow means to pull something, like a truck pulling a car.

hints: The missing word is a number.
To, too and two all sound the same.
Which spelling is the number 2?
items.explanation: Two is the number 2. To and too sound the same but mean different things.

items.prompt: Match the words that sound the same.
hints: Say each word aloud.
Find a word on the other side that sounds exactly the same.
Start with pair. Which word is a fruit that sounds like pair?
items.explanation: Homophones sound the same but have different spellings and meanings, like pair and pear.

items.prompt:
Write write or right in the gap.
Please ___ your name at the top of the page.
hints: What do you do with a pencil and your name?
Right can mean correct, or the opposite of left.
The word you need is about putting words on paper.
items.explanation: Write means to put words on paper. Right means correct, or the opposite of left.

options.why: A tale is a story.
Tall means high, like a tall tree.
A tile is a flat piece on a floor or a roof.

hints: Think about the part of a dog that wags.
Two of these words sound exactly the same.
One of them is a story. Which one is part of an animal?
items.explanation: A tail is the part at the back of an animal. A tale is a story.

items.prompt: Mum used ___ to make the cake.

options.why: A flower is a plant that grows in the garden.
The floor is what you walk on!
Flow means to move along, like water in a river.

hints: What do we put in a cake?
Two of these words sound the same but mean different things.
One is a powder for baking. One grows in a garden.
items.explanation: Flour is the powder used to make cakes and bread. A flower is a plant.

items.prompt: Choose 2 sentences where every word is spelt correctly.

options.text: The wind blue my hat off.
options.why: It should be blew, the past tense of blow. Blue is a colour.
It should be sea, the salty water.
It should be heard. A herd is a group of cows.

hints: Check each word that has a homophone.
Think about what each word means in its sentence.
Look at ate and eight in the first sentence. Does each one fit?
items.explanation: Ate is the past tense of eat and eight is a number, so the first sentence is right. Won is the past tense of win, so the team sentence is right too.

items.prompt:
Write there or their in the gap.
The children hung ___ bags on the hooks.
hints: Whose bags are they?
One word means belonging to them. The other tells you a place.
Ask: is the missing word about a place, or about who owns something?
items.explanation: Their means belonging to them. The bags belong to the children, so we use their.

options.why: A road is what cars and bikes travel on.
Rowed is what you do with oars in a boat.
A rod is a long stick, like a fishing rod.

hints: The missing word is something Ravi did.
It is the past tense of ride.
Today I ride. Yesterday I ...? Find that spelling.
items.explanation: Rode is the past tense of ride. Road and rowed sound the same but mean different things.

options.text: Their are four ducks on the pond.
options.why: Their means belonging to them. This sentence needs a different word.

options.text: There are four ducks on the pond.
There are for ducks on the pond.
options.why: For is not a number. The number is four.

options.text: Their are for ducks on the pond.
options.why: Both their and for are wrong here.

hints: Two words in each sentence have homophones.
There can point to a place or start a sentence. Four is the number 4.
Check the first word of each sentence, then check the number word.
items.explanation: There are is how we say that something is somewhere. Four is the number 4.

items.prompt:
Use to, too or two.
I want ___ come ___!
hints: You need two different words.
One of them means also. One comes before a doing word, as in go and swim.
Fill the first gap. Which word comes before come?
items.explanation: To comes before a verb: to come. Too means also. So the sentence is I want to come too!

items.prompt:
How many words are spelt wrongly?
I herd the sea. Their was a whale with a big tale.

options.why: Look again. More than one word is wrong.
Close! Check every word that has a homophone.
Sea and whale are spelt correctly here.

hints: Look for words that sound like other words.
Check herd, sea, their, whale and tale one at a time.
Herd means a group of cows. Is that what the sentence means?
items.explanation: Herd should be heard, Their should be There, and tale should be tail. Sea and whale are correct, so 3 words are wrong.

hints: The word has five letters.
It belongs to the children, so it shows who owns the coats.
It starts with the letters th and ends with the letters ir.
items.explanation: The word is their. Their shows that something belongs to them. There is a place.
items.sentence: The children put on their coats.
